events.title: Joan of Arc Is Burned at the Stake
events.description: After being convicted of heresy in a politically charged trial, the 19-year-old French military leader Joan of Arc was executed in the marketplace of Rouen, France.
events.significance: Joan had inspired French forces during the Hundred Years' War. Her death made her a martyr, and she was later declared innocent and canonized as a saint.

events.title: Andrew Jackson Kills Charles Dickinson in a Duel
events.description: Future U.S. president Andrew Jackson shot and killed Charles Dickinson in a duel in Kentucky. Dickinson had accused Jackson's wife, Rachel, of bigamy. Jackson was seriously wounded in the exchange.
events.significance: The duel showed the fierce honor culture of the early American republic. It also became part of the fiery reputation that followed Jackson into national politics.

events.title: The Lincoln Memorial Is Dedicated
events.description: The Lincoln Memorial was dedicated in Washington, D.C., in a ceremony attended by thousands. It honors the 16th president with a marble temple and a seated statue.
events.significance: The memorial became one of America's best-known landmarks and a major site for civil rights gatherings, including the 1963 March on Washington.

events.title: The Memorial Day Massacre in Chicago
events.description: Chicago police fired on striking steelworkers and their supporters who were marching toward a Republic Steel plant. Ten people died, and many others were wounded.
events.significance: The killings drew national attention to the violent resistance that workers faced when organizing. They also helped build public support for labor protections.
